<p style="font-size:14px;">
The American Goldfinch (*Spinus tristis*) is a widespread migratory songbird associated with open habitats, including shrublands, forest edges, grasslands, wetlands, and regenerating areas. The species typically relies on early-successional vegetation and areas with abundant herbaceous plants that provide seeds for foraging and suitable nesting habitat. In the boreal region, the availability of open habitats created by natural disturbances, vegetation succession, and landscape management activities can influence habitat suitability. While the American Goldfinch is considered adaptable and can use a variety of modified landscapes, changes in vegetation structure, loss of early-successional habitats, and shifts in disturbance patterns may affect local habitat availability. This vulnerability assessment evaluates potential exposure to landscape changes and assesses factors that may influence habitat conditions for American Goldfinch within the assessment area.
</p>
